space_media_names.description:
Restore word spacing in English media file names, keeping the original characters, numbering and extension.

Only inserts spaces and never changes a character. These are not split: apostrophe contractions (`Couldn't`, `Year's`), all-caps abbreviations (`POV`, `CIM`) and all-caps IDs next to digits (`SPANKPH6`, `ASMR4K`), site domains and the ID right after them (`xvideos.com_abcdefgh`), Pornhub viewkeys and hex IDs (`ph5f8a9bcdef12345`). Words mixing in Cyrillic look-alike letters (`withсum`) are cut as Latin letters; the original characters stay.

`--recompute-batch` recomputes an applied batch with the corrected word splitting: each original name in the log is split again, and rows that differ from the current name go into a review CSV for `--apply --review-csv`.

split_composite_aliases.description:
Split an alias cell that holds several stage names into one person with several names.

r18.dev renders its romanized name field as `current name (former name, former name)`, and import writes one row per field,
so `Ako Momona (Kou Akemi, Mari Koizumi)` became a single alias. As an alias it is dead: no part of it matches a search,
and it is even less fit to be the canonical name. The kana and kanji spellings of the same entity already have their own rows;
only these romanized names are missing, so splitting adds information rather than losing it.

**Only romanized person names are split** (criteria in `peach.entities.COMPOSITE_PERSON_NAME`). The database holds four other,
completely different kinds of "name followed by brackets"; they are left alone and only written to the review CSV for a person:

- `AV DEBUT（本物人妻）`: the brackets hold a label that tells three same-named series apart. Splitting would merge them.
- `アスナ(SAO)`: source disambiguation for character tags; the database has over five hundred.
- `快慢扳机（接稿中）`, `るかぴあ（X：復帰しました）`: the brackets hold commission status or an announcement.
- `kitty(1)`, `Mana(23)`: deduplication suffixes or numbers.

Shapes that cannot be told apart go to review: in the review CSV set `verdict` to `split` (split the alias into several)
or `strip` (replace the canonical name with `target`, keeping the old name as an alias), fill in `target`, then run with `--from-review`.

Splitting cannot be undone. By default only the review CSV is written; `--apply` writes the database and requires `--backup`.

dedupe_entity_links.description:
Merge links on the same entity that point to the same destination into one.

The `UNIQUE(entity_id,url)` constraint on `entity_link` compares only literal strings, but the same destination can
be written many ways:

    http://kawakami-yuu.livedoor.biz      http://kawakami-yuu.livedoor.biz/
    https://x.com/yu_kinao               https://x.com/yu_kinao/status/1221041995415580672
    …/talent/%e6%b6%bc%e6%a3%ae…/        …/talent/%E6%B6%BC%E6%A3%AE…/

The first pair differs by a slash, the second is an account's profile and one of its posts, and the third differs
only in the case of percent escapes. On the profile page, each pair shows up as two identical icons side by side
that lead to the same person. The fetchers are still running, so this is not a one-off cleanup: different sources
naturally write the same account differently, and this path has to stay reusable.

There are two criteria, because "the same destination" means different things for social media and ordinary
websites:
  * Social media is compared by account. Platform plus handle is the identity; whatever follows in the path
    (status, photo, media pages) is still the same person's account.
  * Everything else is compared by host plus path, ignoring a trailing slash. Query strings and fragments still
    count: changing the value of `?id=3` usually means a different page.

Paths are decoded back to bytes before comparing: `%E6` and `%e6` are the same byte, and the paths of Japanese
performer pages are entirely escaped kana, with each source using its own case convention. They are decoded to
bytes rather than text because paths are not guaranteed to be UTF-8.

Within each group, the link with the shortest URL is kept: the shortest is the account profile or site root, which
is the most useful one to open.

Dry-run by default. `--apply` requires `--backup` as well: this is a real database write.

reject_agency.description:
Reject an agency under a given actress: record it in her metadata, remove that membership, and delete the entity too if the agency has no one left.

minnano-av's 「所属事務所」 records only whom she is currently signed with. For people who moved to a personal
management company after retiring, that cell shows her own company (三上悠亜 → 株式会社Miss), and building from it
yields a one-person "agency" that is not an AV agency. Deleting the entity alone is not enough:
`repair_link_labels.py` and `resync_performer_agency.py` write the site's cell back into `metadata.agency`, and
`install_agencies.py` then rebuilds the entity from it. So the rejection is recorded on the person
(`peach.entities.AGENCY_REJECTED`), and these paths skip it when they read it.

The input is a review CSV, one pair per row: `performer,agency,reason[,replacement]`, with names given as
canonical_name. For each row:

1. append `{name, reason, source, decided_at}` to her `metadata.agency_rejected`, without recording the same name
   twice;
2. if `metadata.agency` names exactly this agency, remove it: it is evidence, but a human has judged it invalid;
3. if her membership points to this agency, delete it;
4. if the agency has no members left, delete the entity, with its aliases, links, and external ids removed by
   foreign-key cascade;
5. if `replacement` is given (her actual agency during her AV career, written the same way as the site's cell,
   such as `ONE'S DOUBLE(ワンズダブル)`), reattach her to it: split the current name and aliases with
   `split_name`, create the entity if missing, and write it to `metadata.agency` too, so rerunning
   `install_agencies.py` reaches the same conclusion.

Dry-run by default. `--apply` requires `--backup` as well: this is a real database write.

repair_company_profile_landing.description:
Backfill fix: conclusions without code criteria in company profile batches (ADR-0052, first rule).

Company profile writes accept only the generic criteria of `company_profiles`. This script replays
the criteria against the original page cache recorded in the fetch manifest, and brings what the

repair_entity_links.description:
Audit `entity_link` across the whole database and turn the kinds of fixes that can be confirmed into a plan.

On an actress's profile page, the user opened an official link and landed on the agency's site-wide model list. That
link returned 200, had images, and really was that agency: nothing looked wrong from the backend. His request was
"check all of them and fix them", so this script does not pick out single links; it runs the whole database through
by shape.

## Four kinds of problems, each handled differently

- **Directory pages**: the link lands at the "who's here" level. The fix is to find the person's own page by name in
  the site index.
- **Search pages**: they leave "who is this person over there" to the site's search to guess. Only when the database
  holds that site's id is the link replaced with the direct page; without an id it is marked `保留检索页` for the
  user, and **no direct URL is assembled from the name**: an assembled URL that opens a 404 is the good case; one
  that opens someone else is the real trouble.
- **Plain http**: upgraded when the site offers https.
- **Unescaped HTML entities**: `model.php?alias=x&id=176` came from copying a URL out of page source along with
  the `&`, so the server receives a parameter named `amp;id`, and `id` is lost.

Multiple links for the same site on the same entity are only reported, not changed: they could be two accounts of
the same person, or one could be someone else's; either way a human has to look, and deleting either one would be
the script deciding for the user.

## The check every new URL must pass

The new URL must return 200, **and** the page title must identify this person. The title check cannot be skipped:
list pages also return 200, and without it a batch of people would be rewritten to the same list URL, every one of
which "opens fine".

When only switching protocol or unescaping entities, old and new are the same page, and the title may not contain
the person's name (blog titles are often section names). In that case the check becomes "the new URL's title is
exactly the same as the old one's", which is stronger same-page evidence than a name. If neither holds, it is
written as `未取得` and kept out of the plan.

Rate limiting follows `peach-batch-jobs`: at least `--interval` seconds between two requests to the same domain, a
`--max-requests` cap for the whole run, and fetched pages cached for the run (dozens of links share the same index
page).

Rewrite the labels of actresses' official links by domain ownership, and move agency names to their
own place.

During fetching, `harvest_performer_links.py` read 「所属事務所」 from the minnano-av profile table and
then stuck that name onto every official link found on the same page. In the profile table, 「所属事務所」
and 「公式サイト」 are two separate facts: 白石亚子's agency is T-POWERS, but her 公式サイト is a Prestige
exclusive-actress promo page. So the profile page showed a control speaking for two companies at
once: the text said T-POWERS while the icon and destination were Prestige.

This script does two things in one go:

1. **Labels are written by domain ownership** (`peach.social_links.host_owners`). Whoever owns the
   domain gets their name written; only when the database does not know the owner is the original
   label kept. Facebook and Linktree were previously missing from the platform table and went down
   the official branch; they are moved to social along the way.
2. **Agency names are written to `entity.metadata_json.agency`**, with source and fetch time. It is
   useful information; it just should not live in a link label: a label means "what you see when you
   click through", and cannot hold "whom she is signed with". Actresses change agencies, so this is
   timestamped and the latest overwrites.

Relabeling is reversible (the original values are written to the review CSV, so they can be changed
back), but it is still treated as a real write: by default it only produces the review CSV, and only

Ask again whom these actresses are signed with now, and write the answer back to `entity.metadata_json.agency`.

harvest_directory_links.description:
Social media fetch for directory-style sources: crawl the whole site, match names back to the
database, and check X accounts once more for liveness.

The minnano-av fetcher works by "searching by name". laoshi.ink (686 people) and the agency site
bstar-pro (22 people) go the other way: their page counts are limited, so all pages are fetched once
and cached locally, then each page's name is looked up in the database. Matching costs no network
traffic, the same batch of pages can be compared repeatedly, and "several people with the same name"
and "another account on the same platform" can both be detected offline instead of silently
attaching the wrong person.

The sources themselves may be stale (the user pointed out on 2026-09-02 that copied X / Instagram
accounts are often already suspended, and the person has usually moved to a new account). So each
fetched X account is checked for liveness via its signed-out page: it counts as alive only if it has
og:title and og:image points to profile_images. Signed-out Instagram / TikTok / YouTube pages give
no reliable signal and are marked `unverified`. Only `alive` and `unverified` go into the install
queue; `gone` (likely dead) goes only into the review sheet. Conflict rows are checked on both
sides, and the evidence states whether the database's old account is dead or alive: old one dead and
new one alive is exactly the user's "there's usually a new one".

Verdicts:
    ok            unique match in the database, which has no account on this platform yet
    held          the same account is already in the database (twitter.com/x.com count as one host,
                  handles are case-insensitive)
    conflict      the database has a different account on the same platform: the "cross-check" the user
                  asked for, reported only, never installed
    ambiguous     the page name matches more than one performer
    missed        the page could not be fetched, or the matched person's page has no social links
    fan-account   the X display name says it is a fan account; goes only into the review sheet

Two CSVs are written: `<output>` contains only installable ok rows and feeds install_entity_links.py
directly; `<stem>-review.csv` contains every verdict and is the review file.

jae.tokyo is the third such source: the Japan Adult Expo directory of exhibiting actresses, one set
each for 2014, 2015, and 2017, with materials submitted by the studios themselves; the pages list
the person's blog and official site (`公式ブログ`／`ツイッター`). The directory also carries a portrait, so
this source produces an extra `<stem>-portraits.csv`, picked up by the directory route of
harvest_social_avatars.py: avatars and links come from the same pages and the same name match.

javdb.com (specified by the user on 2026-09-04) is the fourth source, but its entry point is
reversed. The first three sources have limited page counts and can be crawled in full; javdb has no
browsable actress directory, `/actors` shows only a few dozen recommended people, and there is no
paginated entry for all performers. So it searches `/search?f=actor` with the name chain of each
person in the database: the `title` column of the search results lists every spelling of that person
on the site (`三上悠亜, 三上悠亞, 鬼头桃菜`), and only a match leads on to the profile page. The profile page
gives Twitter and Instagram buttons and a 250×250 round avatar.

laoshi.ink and bstar-pro.com are accessed directly (the handshake through the proxy fails, while the
sites themselves are reachable); x.com, jae.tokyo, and javdb.com go through the proxy. bstar-pro's
models.html has an age gate: within the same session, `POST age_check=yes` first, and only then does
GET return the list.

harvest_social_avatars.description:
Social media presence expansion: go from verified X accounts to link-in-bio pages, expand all social links, and
fetch the highest-resolution avatar.

Standard flow (agreed with the user on 2026-09-02): social links and avatars are two outputs of the same chain:

    X/Twitter in entity_link (installed by the minnano-av pipeline and reviewed by a human)
      → X signed-out page: og:image gives the person's avatar, og:title gives the display name (evidence for
        the name gate), and plain-text links in the bio give the link-in-bio page
      → link-in-bio page (lit.link / linktr.ee / allmylinks / twpf.jp): every external link, rendered
        server-side: Instagram, TikTok, Threads, Fantia, DMM/MGStage searches...
      → deduplicate identical avatars across social platforms and take the largest, sharpest one.

Three outputs:
  1) a link install queue CSV (feeds install_entity_links.py; only rows that pass the name gate);
  2) rows that fail the gate go into a review CSV, recorded but not installed;
  3) an avatar candidate CSV (performer-avatar-candidate- prefix, readable by the review page as usual), whose
     winners passing both quality and identity are installed into generated/avatars under `--apply`; the user has
     explicitly authorized "avatars on different social platforms are usually the same; take the largest and
     sharpest, and if that doesn't work, add it to review". Those below the auto-install bar still go into the
     review queue for a human to approve on the review page.

The default is a dry run: only the three CSVs above are produced, and not a single byte is written to disk. What gets
installed wrongly is a face, and faces are exactly why the review queue exists (the KRONE case of "right person,
wrong page" was this kind), so like every other write script in the repository, writing to disk requires an
explicit `--apply`.

`--apply` only swaps in something better: before writing, the image on disk is measured with the same yardstick
(`rank_key`), and it is not overwritten unless the face is larger. The avatar directory is shared by several
pipelines, and this script's candidate pool is not necessarily better than what others installed.

Avatar sources (available signed out; where none can be fetched, only the link is recorded and no avatar produced):
  X          profile_images original (no size suffix), falling back to _400x400 / _200x200
  lit.link   the person's profile icon node and the original avatar declared by the page
  babepedia  /pics/<Babe>.jpg — creator entities use matching rows in babepedia-candidates.csv
  jae        portraits submitted by studios themselves in the Japan Adult Expo directory — use matching
             rows in jae-performer-links-portraits.csv produced by harvest_directory_links.py
Signed-out Instagram pages give no avatar image, and TikTok's oembed avatar is only about a hundred pixels; both
record the link only.

The identity gate is a chain of checks: minnano-av redirect installed into the database → X page og:title matches
the name chain → link-in-bio page title/body matches the name chain. Every hop has name evidence; wherever the
chain breaks, outputs after that hop go only to review and are never written automatically.

install_entity_links.description:
Install reviewed entity links into the database's `entity_link`.

This script repairs a broken path, not a new feature. The `entity_link` table, the `links` contract of `q_entity`,
favicon rendering on profile pages, and non-clickable sensitive sources were all written back in 2026-08; the only
thing missing was "how reviewed results get into the database". As a result, 8178 entities had only 5 links, and none
of the 14 handles in `studio-x-handles.csv` that a human had confirmed by looking at images had taken effect:
fetched, reviewed, with no install path. This is the fourth time the same pattern has appeared in this repository
(`creator_tags`, `studio_logos`, and `performer_avatars` each did it once).

Dry-run by default, printing only the plan. `--apply` requires `--backup` as well: this is a real database write.
Writes are idempotent (`UNIQUE(entity_id,url)`), so rerunning does not create duplicate rows.

harvest_agency_rosters.description:
Fill in agency memberships from minnano-av agency rosters: who belongs to an agency, not just which agency a person belongs to.

All 200 memberships in the database come from the 「所属事務所」 row on actress pages, asked one person at a time.
That path only reaches people who have already been asked: `harvest_performer_links.py` defaults to
`--min-assets 3`, so only 200 of 559 performers have been asked, and the rest still have no membership. The agency
page's "Performers" roster has to answer the reverse question, and right now it shows only the part that was asked,
making it look as though the agency has three people.

The roster page is the answer to that reverse question: `actress_list.php?production=<id>` lists 30 people per page,
and its JSON-LD carries the agency's total headcount (マインズ: 249, measured 2026-09-05). Fetching one agency at a
time saves two orders of magnitude of requests compared with asking person by person.

**The id can only be obtained through a person.** The site has no agency index page; the id appears only in the
internal link in the 「所属事務所」 cell of an actress page. So known members of the agency are searched first,
landing on an actress page, reading the id, and checking that the name in that cell really is this agency;
attaching on the strength of a number alone means a mistake would be invisible in the review file. If it cannot be
confirmed, it is recorded as 「未取得」 (not fetched); no guessing. The id obtained is written to
`entity_external_ref`, so the next run does not have to ask again.

**Names on the roster must be matched back to the database.** A performer's canonical name in the database is in
Simplified Chinese (`凉森玲梦`), with the Japanese spelling in `entity_alias` (`涼森れむ`), so names must be matched
together with aliases. Unmatched names are recorded as 「不在库」 (not in library): people this agency has and we do
not, which is not an error. A spelling that matches two people is recorded as 「重名」 (duplicate name) and left for a
human to decide.

**People who already have a membership are left alone.** The `entity_membership` primary key is on the member side,
so a person has only one current membership. If the roster says this person belongs to A and the database says B,
that is either a transfer or a fetch error, and both need a human: it is recorded as 「另有归属」 (other
membership), and `--apply` does not touch it.

Dry-run by default, producing only the review CSV. `--apply` requires `--backup` as well: this is a real database
write.

fetch_fc2_metadata.description:
Fetch FC2 video metadata and human-made tags from the comment sections on fc2cmadb.

FC2 has no code system like JAV; official pages carry only the titles sellers write themselves, and performers are
rarely listed. fc2cmadb's value is not the main text but the **comment section**: users maintain two kinds of tags
there over the long term.

Performer tags, `<video_id>　<名前>`, separated by a full-width space; one line can list several performers:

    2724256　未歩なな　皐月
    1934545　ゆう

Equivalence tags, which map releases of the same content under different video_ids to each other:

    3312576-4 = 2471432 = 3090722-1 = 4605413

Equivalence is the criterion for compilations, and the main reason this script exists. `FC2PPV-3312576` is a
21-part compilation, stored locally as parts like `FC2PPV-3312576-1.mp4`. **A compilation cover must never be
applied to each part**: that would make 21 videos with different content show the same image. So when something is
judged to be a compilation, `cover_url` is left empty and the note says so, letting the parts fall back to their
own thumbnails.

The pages are Laravel + Inertia, with data in `<script type="application/json">`, so no HTML parsing is needed.
Requests carry the Cookie the user pasted into the fetch settings, getting the page as the signed-in user sees it.
Parsing of page URLs, props, and comment tags lives in the site parser `peach.sources.fc2cmadb`; this script only
handles aggregation, the harvest table, and review candidates.

Comments are written by anonymous users and are always treated only as candidates: the output is a CSV for human
review, and truth fields are never touched. When the same performer name is mentioned by two or more independent
comments, confidence is higher; this is recorded in `performer_votes`.

**Only video pages already in the library are fetched, but every comment on each page is kept.** One page of
comments often tags performers for dozens of video_ids, of which only two or three match locally; keeping only the
matching ones would throw away the value of the comment section. So there are three outputs: a candidate CSV per
local asset (for the review page), a full harvest CSV aggregated by video_id, and the raw comments as JSONL. The raw
text is kept because the regexes that parse the tags will certainly miss some way of writing them, and with the raw
text there is no need to crawl again for that.

harvest_performer_links.description:
Fetch actresses' social media and agency links from minnano-av. The "refer to beeg's social links" the user asked for has no source in the database: the Stash import ran long ago, and 567 performers brought along only 2 URLs, because the local Stash never stored those fields. minnano-av is currently the only entry point that leads from an actress's name to social media and agencies; `docs/reference-snapshots/minnano-av-official-portraits.md` records exactly this, and the "search form for locating a page from an actress's name" in that record was marked as not fetched at the time; this script obtains it. **Only redirects are trusted.** `search_result.php?search_scope=actress&search_word=` has three outcomes: a unique match redirects to `actressNNN.html`; multiple matches or no match both stay on the search page, titled 「「」のAV女優検索結果」. value

harvest_maker_directories.description:
Fetch official wordmarks from the label directories of studios and distribution platforms, producing reviewable `LOGO_SOURCES` candidates.

The JAE batch in `LOGO_SOURCES` was collected by hand from the expo directory: 26 labels, each checked by eye. These
directories easily run to dozens or hundreds of labels; copying them by hand is impractical, but volume is no reason
to skip confirmation either, so this script produces only candidates and evidence, and writing to `LOGO_SOURCES`
still happens after a person has looked.

**Directories give Japanese names, while the database often records English brand names** (`ムーディーズ` vs
`MOODYZ`); the only stable bridge between the two is the romanized slug in the file name (such as `aroma.gif`). So
matching runs four ways, and each writes its criterion into the review file's `how` column: the hundreds that do not
match are not failures but labels the database does not have yet, and their wordmarks now have a source. **The
review file includes unmatched entries by default**, and that is this script's main output: someone else's database
does not hold the same labels as this machine's, so keeping the whole directory lets another library match against
it too.

What is stored is the directory entry point rather than hundreds of image URLs. KMP's file names carry timestamps
(`file/label_1727404339.png`), so the URL changes whenever a label changes its logo; rerunning from the entry point
always gets the current version.

This script does not judge images. The criteria for size, content ratio, and square mark versus wordmark already
exist in `harvest_studio_icons.py`; a second copy would only conflict with it.

install_agencies.description:
Turn agency names in `entity.metadata_json.agency` into entities and memberships.

Agencies used to be just a string in actress entity metadata. A string cannot be searched or opened, and cannot
answer the reverse question: "who is in Capsule Agency?" Like labels and series, an agency is a canonical identity
with a name, an official site, and members; the only thing missing was a `kind`. Migration 0025 added `agency` and
`entity_membership`, and this script moves the 200 memberships already fetched into them.

The fetched original text stays in `metadata.agency`: that is the evidence (which site, when it was fetched), and the
entity is the conclusion. Keeping both means a wrong conclusion can be traced back.

Parentheses in names are split by one rule: outside the parentheses is the current name, and what is inside or
follows them is a reading or former name, always kept as an alias. `GG(旧・Prime Agency)` has the current name
`GG`, while a different `Prime Agency` is still operating; when a former name collides with another agency's
current name, no alias is written, and it is only reported for a human to decide.

Dry-run by default. `--apply` requires `--backup` as well: this is a real database write.

seed_pack.description:
Export and import of entity fact seed packs (ADR-0073).

    seed_pack.py export --version 2026-10-23.1
    seed_pack.py validate
    seed_pack.py import
    seed_pack.py import --apply --backup peach-data/database/ledger.pre-seed-<timestamp>.db

`export` only reads the database and by default writes to the app resource
`resources/seed/entities.json`, which a maintainer reviews and ships with the release; format 2
keeps source confidence, inherits cumulative explicit revocations, and binds the version and import
task with a content digest. Changed content must advance the version and revision; different content
under the same version, or a rolled-back revision, is rejected. `validate` only checks the pack,
without opening the database. `import` is dry-run by default and only reports how much it would fill
in; `--apply` requires `--backup` as well. To revert: `revert_auto_landing.py --source auto:seed`.

changelog.description:
Changelog: draft from Conventional Commits, and finalize the Unreleased section at release time.

Format follows Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 (https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and version numbers
follow Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html): `## [未发布]` is
always present, each release gets a section `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD`, group headings are fixed, and
compare links go at the bottom.

The draft groups commits by subject, and a person must rewrite the wording into something users
understand: the spec's first principle is that a changelog is written for humans, not a dump of
`git log`. Commits that only touch the development process (`docs`, `test`, `chore`, `refactor`)
stay out. At release, human-polished content in the Unreleased section moves into the version
section as a whole; the draft is a fallback only when that section is empty.

Each entry also carries an area tag (`- **播放**：…`): group headings sort by the nature of the change,
tags by the area users see. Recognized scopes are replaced with tags automatically; draft entries
still carrying an English scope are waiting for someone to pick a tag.

    python scripts/changelog.py                                # draft the unreleased range
    python scripts/changelog.py --range v0.16.0..v0.27.1       # draft any range
    python scripts/changelog.py --release 0.30.0 --apply       # finalize Unreleased as 0.30.0
    python scripts/changelog.py --notes 0.30.0 --to NOTES.md   # generate this version's Release notes

check_reference_updates.description:
Check drift between mutable external Markdown and Peach's locked snapshots.

Each source is tiered by `cadence`: `weekly` covers upstreams that Peach code consumes directly or copies verbatim,
checked together with the weekly Dependabot updates; `monthly` covers design guidelines and algorithm references;
`quarterly` covers READMEs of similar products, left for full research rounds; `manual` is checked only when named
with `--source`. `volatile` marks web pages whose fetched bytes differ every time; these sources are matched only by
Git revision. `pins` are runtime dependencies pinned in the manifest by 40-character sha, which Dependabot cannot
bump; this script reports whether their upstream has moved ahead.

release_due.description:
Asked once at the end of a session: is it time to ship the next version? If not, say nothing at all.

The criterion itself lives in `changelog.due()`; this script only decides when to ask, whom to ask,
and how many times. It hooks onto the end of a session because release timing has no automatic
trigger: it belongs to neither a commit nor an integration, and relies entirely on someone
remembering one day to count changelog entries. `integrate` output already carries the same
judgment, but only when a branch happens to land, and the days in a week without integration are
exactly when it is easiest to forget.

Four gates first block occasions that should stay silent; if any one of them fails, it exits
silently:

1. **Not in the main checkout**: workers in isolated worktrees do not release; reminding them
   reminds the wrong person.
2. **Not on master**: releases only go out from the main line; a reminder received on another branch
   cannot be acted on.
3. **Working tree not clean**: no release is possible right now; ask again at the next wrap-up,
   after this round of changes lands.
4. **Already asked for this version**: latched to the master sha, asking only once per sha. Once
   master moves forward, new things have accumulated, and asking again then is right.

Usage (`--hook-event` is for the Claude and Codex Stop hooks; for a manual check, use the form
without arguments):

    python scripts/release_due.py                  # print the judgment, read-only, latch untouched
    python scripts/release_due.py --hook-event     # read hook JSON from stdin, reply with systemMessage

release_tag.description:
Version bump and version tag: the only entry point for releases.

A release takes two commands, with one human confirmation in between:

    python scripts/release_tag.py --bump auto --apply   # bump the version, draft that section
    #  → check the wording of the new section in `CHANGELOG.md`: the only notes users read
    python scripts/release_tag.py --ship --apply        # commit, push, wait for CI, tag,
                                                        # then repoint README links once artifacts exist

There is only one confirmation point; the script enforces every other check: `--ship` refuses to
carry other changes, refuses to tag before Test turns green, and picks up where it left off when
rerun after stopping midway. The only decision for a person is whether the wording is right, not
which step the process has reached.

Version numbers change only here: every `X.Y.Z` corresponds to a downloadable artifact, while
day-to-day integrated commits are identified by commit (ADR-0012).

check_public_text.description:
Before text goes public, check two things: serialized lists of collection details, and insider terms
that outside readers cannot follow.

PRs, issues, comments, and commit messages are all public on GitHub, and old versions stay in the
edit history after editing. The one or two codes, prefixes, or tags the problem itself needs are
fine; listing codes, people's names, or title fragments from the database in a string gets blocked.
The check only reads the local database (SQLite `mode=ro`); the repository carries no collection
data, and machines without a database (CI, other contributors) always pass.

Readers of PRs, issues, and comments are community contributors and users: item numbers from
feedback summaries, batch numbers and rounds from task assignments, relative phrases that do not say
what they refer to, such as "remaining modules" or "the topmost PR", and local delivery-process
wording (worktree, `ready` output, and so on) mean nothing to them; see `insider_terms`. This part
does not look at the database, nor does it check commit messages: commits that change worktree
scripts naturally have to mention worktrees.

When truly necessary, write a line `peach-public-text: <reason>` in the body to let it through.

Usage:
    python scripts/check_public_text.py FILE...      # check files; `-` reads stdin
    python scripts/check_public_text.py --hook-event # Claude PreToolUse hook; blocks gh publishing

Backfill fix: single-word romanized aliases written by Western profile pages
(`performer_alias_followup.latin_rejection`).

Single words like `Lena`, `Mara`, and `Kitten` are not stage names, and many people share them;
merging performers on a unique alias match would attach someone else to her. This script deletes
aliases written by the specified source that the current criteria reject. Aliases are kept when the
page's main name is itself a single word: when `--plan` is given, each person's `matched_name` is
read from the fetch manifest.

By default it only lists the plan (opening the database read-only); `--apply` requires `--backup` as
well.

check_pr_identity.fix:
First set your own identity, then rewrite these commits and force-push the PR branch:
  git config user.name "<your name>"
  git config user.email "<your email>"
  git rebase -r <base> --exec "git commit --amend --no-edit --reset-author"
  git push --force-with-lease
<base> is the PR's target branch, e.g. upstream/master.
